_comment: Index mapping for the Conzent support knowledge base.
Create as conzent-kb-v2 and alias conzent-kb to it, so the existing
Legacy fields kept for compatibility: title, body, tags, audience, source, reviewed, createdAt.
Set body_vector dims to match your embedding model (768 = e5-base / gte-base, 1024 = e5-large,
1536 = OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). Change BOTH vector fields together.

synonyms: banner, cookie banner, cookie notice, consent banner, popup
preference center, preference centre, settings panel, second layer
gcm, google consent mode, consent mode
tcf, iab tcf, transparency and consent framework
dns, do not sell, do not sell or share
website key, site key, api key, data-key
script, snippet, tag, embed code, install code
consent log, consent record, audit trail, consent proof
self-hosted, oci, on-premise, on premise, community edition
revisit button, floating button, reopen banner

conzent_search._comment: search-time only: expands the query, not the index

id._comment: stable slug, e.g. banner.general — mirrored into _id

body._comment: full Markdown body of the article (frontmatter stripped)

summary._comment: first paragraph of 'What it does' — safe for the agent to quote verbatim

questions._comment: anticipated user phrasings — boost this field hard, it is the highest-signal match

fields_covered._comment: flat list of every UI control name in the article — lets 'what is X toggle' resolve

knowledgebase._comment: Which knowledge base this document ships in — one per articles/ folder. Filter on this to scope retrieval to a single KB.

edition._comment: cloud | self-hosted — filter before answering, pages differ per edition

audience._comment: customer | agency | admin | both (legacy value written by KnowledgeBaseService)

plan._comment: any | paid | business — Cloud plan gate for the feature

source._comment: document | transcript | manual — legacy field, filtered on by the admin KB list

content_hash._comment: sha256 of the body — importer skips re-embedding unchanged articles

questions_vector._comment: embedding of the joined questions list — matches conversational phrasing better than the body
